title: Ship-time consumption resolves triage top_n ids only — a triage-decomposed lane NEVER consumes its dispatched item (lane-scope todo_ids ignored), silently defeating #466 on most substantial lanes
summary: Cycle-1515 (verified by code+artifact trace): lane-scope.json todo_ids=[park-consume-releases-continuation-binding] matched the tracked inbox file's .id exactly, but triage decomposed the work into 3 sub-ids (registry-release-on-park-consume, planner-adoption-live-item-guard, continuation-operator-cli) and consumeCommittedItems extracts ids ONLY from triage-decision.json top_n/skip_shipped — FindFileByTaskID missed 3x, each an intentionally-silent ErrNotFound continue. The PASS red=0 ship 868b8cf8 carried zero inbox changes; the item stayed pickable until a console commit 4 minutes later. Cycle-1516's parent re-pick was the same class from the other side. Since triage decomposition is the NORM on substantial items, #466's consumption is silently defeated on exactly the lanes that matter most.
root_cause: Two id namespaces: the dispatched item's identity (lane-scope.json todo_ids == tracked file .id) vs triage's decomposed working ids (top_n). consumeCommittedItems reads only the latter; the linkage back to the dispatched identity is never consulted.
fix: In consumeCommittedItems, union the id set: extractIDs(triage-decision) ∪ laneScope.TodoIDs (core.loadLaneScope already exists and is used by continuation adoption — reuse, single-source). The dispatched item id is the PRIMARY consumption target; triage sub-ids remain for skip_shipped attribution. Red-first: fixture with lane-scope id X + triage top_n [X1,X2] and a tracked inbox item .id==X — the PASS ship must consume X in-commit (pins the cycle-1515 shape). Guard: ids in lane-scope but NOT claimed/tracked no-op as today.
acceptance: Decomposed-lane PASS ship consumes the dispatched item in-commit (red-first, cycle-1515 shape).
Sanctioned-drift + provenance checks (#473) exercise on the consumed pair.
